jack_acme: Hey team — after the model swap this morning our /parse-order ingest is throwing a hard error in prod. Parser fails with `TypeError: expected list for \"items\", got object` for about 30% of responses. Happening across multiple customers. Example response below.

jack_acme: ```json
{
  \"order_id\": \"ORD-98342\",
  \"items\": {
    \"0\": {\"sku\": \"A12\", \"qty\": 1},
    \"1\": {\"sku\": \"B34\", \"qty\": 2}
  },
  \"total\": 39.99
}
```

sophia_cs: Thanks for the heads up — can you paste the model name in the calls that failed and one failing request id? Also did you see this immediately after the model swap time?

jack_acme: model: \"redwood-structured-v2\" in the failed traces. One request id: req_01GH9ZK2. Yes it started ~10:12 UTC right after the deploy that changed the default model for that route.

anja_eng: I pulled the trace for req_01GH9ZK2. Response shows the runtime returned an object keyed by indexes rather than an array. Looks like the new model variant is emitting an enveloped sequence form. Not seeing the same behavior in our smoke tests though.

anja_eng: quick diff of the output shapes: old model -> \"items\": [ {...}, {...} ] ; new model -> \"items\": { \"0\": {...}, \"1\": {...} }

mike_infra: deploy-bot shows a model rotation at 10:10 UTC for the customer routing policy (auto-rotate -> redwood-structured-v2). No other infra changes.

sophia_cs: Can you confirm whether customers who pinned model versions are affected? Jack, are you on hosted or dedicated?

jack_acme: We're on hosted API, not pinned. We rolled our own parser that strictly enforces the JSON schema and immediately throws on non-array. For now we had to pause ingestion.

anja_eng: Root cause hypothesis: the generator is now returning sequence-like structures as maps when it thinks numeric keys are sufficient (compact indexing optimization). It's a model-behavior change, not a downstream serializer bug. We'll reproduce locally.

anja_eng: Repro steps I'm trying: 1) call same prompt with redwood-structured-v1 vs redwood-structured-v2 2) compare tokenization/formatting flags (allow_sparse_sequence) 3) run with runtime flag `preserve_list_semantics=true`

jack_acme: If you need a quick mitigation for us: can you route our requests back to redwood-structured-v1? We need ingestion flowing.

mike_infra: I can push a temporary routing override for this customer's project to pin the model back to redwood-structured-v1 for the next 2 hours. Doing that now. Will confirm when active.

deploy-bot: AUTOMATION: route_override applied -> project: acme-corp, model: redwood-structured-v1, expires: 2h (by mike_infra)

jack_acme: Thanks, routing override fixed throughput immediately. Parser resumed normal processing.

anja_eng: We have a repro and will open a model compatibility ticket with the model team. Possible fixes: 1) update model's structured-output formatter to prefer arrays for numeric sequences, 2) runtime server normalize numeric-keyed objects into arrays when schema expects an array. The latter is faster to ship as runtime patch.

sophia_cs: I'll keep the customer notified. Jack — we'll follow up with timeline for the runtime patch and a postmortem of the model swap process to avoid silent format changes for strict-schema customers.

jack_acme: Appreciate it. Also posting the failing request payload and logs to the support ticket (TKT-5421). Will add any additional examples if we see more.

anja_eng: Filed model-compat issue: MCOMP-1289. Next steps: 1) add an automated schema-compat smoke test to the model onboarding job; 2) ship runtime normalization fallback; 3) add a deploy guard to flag model variants that change top-level container types.

sophia_cs: Good plan. I'll link MCOMP-1289 into the support ticket and set expectation with customer for 48-72h ETA on a proper fix.

jack_acme: OK thanks everyone :thumbsup:
